title: Trump Impersonator Steals the Show at Ottawa Press Dinner
excerpt: A comedy sketch of Donald Trump had Ottawa’s political elite in stitches, highlighted by Prime Minister Carney’s amused watch.
body:
## A Night of Laughter in Ottawa
At a parliamentary press gallery dinner in Ottawa, Prime Minister Justin Carney found himself sharing the stage with a familiar face from Canadian satire. Comedian Mark Critch, best known for his role on the sketch series *This Hour Has 22 Minutes*, strutted out in a deliberately ill‑fitting suit and a coiffed wig to impersonate former U.S. President Donald Trump. The audience—comprising politicians, journalists and a handful of curious onlookers—burst into raucous applause as the performer launched into a tongue‑in‑cheek critique of the former president’s trade war and, in a surprising twist, his alleged fascination with men’s backsides.

## Satire Meets Politics
Critch’s routine leaned heavily on the exaggerated bravado that has become synonymous with Trump’s public persona. He poked fun at the trade conflict that the U.S. leader initiated, riffing on the economic fallout while keeping the tone light enough for a mixed crowd. The highlight, however, was a cheeky jab at Trump’s rumored preoccupation with “men’s backsides,” a line that drew a fresh wave of laughter and underscored the evening’s playful spirit. Throughout the act, Carney watched from the side, his expression a blend of amusement and bemusement as the satire unfolded.

## Why It Matters
While the event was primarily a social gathering for the press corps, the performance underscored how political comedy can bridge borders. By bringing a Canadian take on an American political figure to a domestic audience, the sketch reminded everyone that humor remains a potent tool for commentary, especially in a setting where journalists and lawmakers mingle. The Guardian reported on the incident, noting the audience’s enthusiastic response and the way the impersonation added a memorable twist to an otherwise routine diplomatic dinner.

The night concluded with applause and a sense that, even in formal settings, a good laugh can ease the tension of international politics.
